name: California
hook: The Gold Rush state, asked through its cities, parks and extremes.

facts.label: the 31st state
facts.statement: California joined the Union in 1850 and is now the most populous state in the country.

facts.label: the Gold Rush
facts.statement: James Marshall found gold at Coloma in 1848, setting off the Gold Rush that swelled California's population.

facts.label: Death Valley
facts.statement: Death Valley holds the record for the hottest temperature in North America: 134 degrees Fahrenheit on July 10, 1913.

facts.label: Yosemite
facts.statement: Yosemite is the East-Central California national park with Badger Pass and the Grand Canyon of the Tuolumne.

facts.label: San Francisco
facts.statement: San Francisco was named for its bay, which was named for St. Francis of Assisi.

facts.label: Sacramento
facts.statement: Sacramento, the state capital, grew during the Gold Rush and was the western end of the Pony Express and the transcontinental railroad.

facts.label: Stanford
facts.statement: Stanford University, built on Leland Stanford's farm, is called "The Farm"; Herbert Hoover managed its first football team.
